_base_branch_comment: The branch this repo's own work is measured against: what
'changed files' is relative to, what counts as already-published
history, and what branch generated links should point at.
This is NOT the same question as 'what is the configured default
branch', even though the two usually have the same answer. They
diverge the moment a repo pins its work to a branch that is not
the default -- which is exactly what this repo does while
precedent-beta-v01 is unmerged. Tools that resolved
refs/remotes/origin/HEAD were asking the first question while
meaning the second, and were silently wrong here for weeks.
Set this to 'main' when Morgan or Alex says work moves there -- NOT
at a merge of precedent-beta-v01 into main, which happened 2026-09-14
and recurs regularly while work keeps landing here (Morgan, 2026-09-14).
THE CATALOGUE'S OWN LINKS MOVE WITH IT:
every practice file that references something outside practices/ does
so as an absolute URL carrying this branch name (practice:
practice-links-travel), so changing this value without rewriting them
leaves every one of them (134 at the landing) pointing at a branch
nobody publishes from.
precedent_check.py's practice-links-travel check fails on exactly that
mismatch, so the fold-in is told; it is one sed across practices/.
A consumer repo with no pin should
declare its own default here rather than omit the key: an absent
value falls back to origin/HEAD, which is the behaviour this
exists to stop relying on.

Renamed from precedent-beta-v01 to staging on 2026-09-25 (spec/BRANCH_TIERS_PLAN.md; Morgan: "we should always call the staging one staging including renaming that branch to staging in precedent", strength: decided; Alex approving, relayed by Morgan). precedent-beta-v01 is kept, fast-forwarded to staging by every Promote, so an install still pinned to it updates onto the engine that names staging.
_branch_stale_days_comment: How old a MERGED, undeleted branch has to be before the very deep
check's branch sweep marks it stale (tools/very_deep_check.py). It
sorts the deletion list; it never decides whether a branch is safe to
delete, which the ancestor test already proved for every row in it.
Declared here rather than compiled into the engine because a threshold
nobody decided is doctrine (practice: constants-are-risk-inputs), and
because the right number is a property of how a repo works -- a repo
with a weekly release wants a smaller one than this.
30 HERE, against an engine default of 90, and the difference is the
whole reason this is a declared value. Measured 2026-09-10 across this
repo's 69 merged-and-undeleted branches: median age 3 days, oldest 39.
At 90 the stale list is empty and the feature is inert here; at 30 it
separates the handful nobody has touched in a month from the pile
merged this week. The engine keeps 90 because an adopting repo that
has declared nothing should get the conservative number.
What is NOT claimed: that 30 is correct. Nobody has data on how long a
merged branch sits before it stops meaning anything, and inventing one
would be exactly what no-invented-specifics forbids. It is a value
picked to fit a measured distribution, and it is one line to change.
`--stale-days N` overrides it for a single run; omitting the key falls
back to very_deep_check.STALE_DAYS_DEFAULT.
_session_window_days_comment: How far back the very deep check's live-session sweep looks when it
asks what has happened in this repository recently
(tools/very_deep_check.py's LIVE SESSIONS section). It bounds the repo
half -- commits, branches and dirty trees -- that a session holds the
Declared rather than compiled in, for the same reason as
branch_stale_days above: a number nobody decided is doctrine
reaches is a property of how fast a repo works.
14 matches the engine default here, deliberately: it is longer than any
single session and longer than a weekend either side of one, so work
begun on a Friday and abandoned on the Monday is still in the window on
the Wednesday after. What is NOT claimed is that 14 is correct -- no
measurement here supports a number, and inventing one would be what
no-invented-specifics forbids. `--session-days N` overrides it for a

_stale_checkout_hours_comment: How much OLDER than origin this checkout may be before the freshness
guard stops calling it 'behind' and starts calling it STALE
(.claude/hooks/freshness-guard.sh). Measured as the gap between the two
tips' commit times, not as a commit count: a count says nothing about
risk, and the person reading the warning judges it on time.
Declared here rather than compiled into the hook because a threshold
24 because that is where Morgan drew the line, 2026-09-13, in his own
framing: an hour behind and 'chances are not much changed'; a few days
behind and 'chances are a lot did, thus increasing the risk of
problems'. What is NOT claimed is that 24 is measured -- nothing here
counts how often a day-old checkout actually caused a problem, and
inventing such a figure is what no-invented-specifics forbids. It is a
line drawn at the boundary he named, and it is one line to change.
`git config precedent.freshness.staleHours N` overrides it for a single
checkout; omitting the key, or having no python3 on the hook path,
falls back to the guard's own 24.
_fallback_timezone_comment: The zone used to stamp commits and generated dates when NOBODY'S own
zone could be resolved -- no PRECEDENT_COMMIT_TZ, no identity.json
reachable, no TZ in the environment. Declared by Morgan, 2026-09-09.
It is APPLIED and never ENFORCED. Applied, because the alternative is
not 'no zone' -- it is the container's UTC, silently, and a record
stamped +0000 by somebody who is not in UTC cannot be ordered against
anyone else's. Any consistent real offset restores the ordering. Never
enforced, because refusing a person's commit over a zone THEY never
declared would block real work on a value they never saw; declaring a
timezone in your own identity.json is what makes it yours and checked.
This is the REPO-level rung of the ladder in tools/precedent_time.py --
a person's zone is person-level and belongs in their identity.json,
while the answer for a person this project could not identify is the
repository's to choose. An adopting repo sets its own here rather than
editing the vendored engine (practice: layered-practice-packs).
Omitting the key falls back to precedent_time.FALLBACK_TZ, which is the
same value; the engine's last resort is deliberately a real zone rather
than UTC, for the reason in the first paragraph.
Read by tools/precedent_time.py and .claude/hooks/commit-identity.sh.
practice: timestamps-carry-offset, registry-source-of-truth.
_writeup_dir_comment: Where a 'Write it up' report is committed in this repository (practice:
write-it-up). Declared by Morgan, 2026-09-26: any session in any repo
running this layer can write these, so they need one known place rather
spec/ here, and spec/ is also what a repo gets when it omits the key.
A repo whose spec/ already means something else -- a Ruby project's
RSpec suite is the common case -- declares its own directory here.
The person naming another place for one write-up overrides it for that
_comment: The practice sources in force in this repository. Precedent is its own
consumer: the universal set it publishes is the set it runs on.
A shared repository may declare universal and shared sources ONLY -- a
person's individual set is declared in their own user-level config, so
that naming it here cannot leak its existence to everyone on the team.
See tools/precedent_resolve.py for the resolution and precedence rules.
The shared sources below are real (level `shared`; `team` was the word
until 2026-09-18 and still reads): precedent-team-repo-maintenance IS this
repo's own maintaining team's conventions (Morgan and Alex). Declared
2026-09-02 by the phase-5 deep-check follow-up -- see
spec/PHASE5_DEEPCHECK.md's 'wiring precedent-team-repo-maintenance into
BestPractice' note for what this does and does not change: it makes
precedent_resolve.py (run from a checkout with a sibling clone of that
repo, or precedent_materialize.py against a real checkout) correctly
resolve this repo's own real team source, for the first time. It does
NOT reach this repo's generated AGENTS.md loader block, and that is
deliberate -- see the visibility note below. build_views.py renders the
block from every source a repo declares, but skips private-level sources
in a repo declaring visibility: public, which this one is. MAP.md and
GLOSSARY.md are single-source in every repo, public or not: they document
the catalogue this repo publishes, not the rules it happens to follow.
THREE team sets, not one, since 2026-09-09 -- the subject split. On
2026-09-09 the maintainers' set was sorted by SUBJECT: of its 40
practices, 19 were about something other than maintaining a repository,
and they moved to precedent-team-writing (the craft of writing for a
human reader) and precedent-team-working-style (how a session paces work
with the person). This file was not updated with them, so for the rest
of that day this repository declared one set and resolved 21 of the 40
rules it used to -- including, by the split's own account, the only two
that fire on every turn of every session. Nothing announced that: every
moved practice keeps a deduplicated file in the old set naming where it
went, which is what a session sees INSTEAD of the rule.
The rule for which sets a repo declares is the one the split
established: a set about a KIND OF WORK is declared by everyone who does
that work, whatever team they are on; a set about running a kind of
repository is declared only by repositories of that kind. This repo is a
maintained repository AND is almost entirely prose written for human
readers, so it takes all three.
Two team sources claiming one slug is a hard refusal (nothing orders two
sources at the same level), so adding sets is not free -- the split
verified no collisions across every set it covered before this became
declarable at all. See INSTALL.md's team-sets table and TODO.md's
split-team-sets-by-subject item.
The repo-local source below (declared 2026-09-03, after the PR #89
merge-target incident) is this repo's own temporary practice: every
PR targets staging (then precedent-beta-v01), never main, until Morgan
or Alex says work moves to main. It reaches the generated loader block
now -- it lives in this repo's own tree, so nothing about it is private;
AGENTS.md's hand-authored 'Working in
this repo' section still states the rule outright as well, since a
temporary rule this sharp is worth saying twice. See local/practices/ and
PRACTICE_ENGINE_PLAN.md's 'Source' section for the path: "local"
convention this follows. Its NAME is fixed to "local" by the same
convention -- see spec/SOURCE_NAMING.md and practices/source-naming.md.
`not_binding` (added 2026-09-06) is how this repo says a practice is IN
FORCE at its source but does NOT bind this repository -- a rule about a
different KIND of repo, e.g. one a single person authors alone. Shape:
"not_binding": [{"slug": "...", "reason": "why it does not bind"}]
The reason is mandatory: an exemption nobody argued for is the same
silence this mechanism replaces. A `severity: blocking` practice cannot
be exempted at all, and an entry naming a slug nothing puts in force is
reported as stale. See decisions/2026-09-06-precedent-binds-itself.md
and tools/precedent_resolve.py's load_not_binding().
It is deliberately EMPTY here for now: populating it needs the private
sources resolved, and an exemption for a practice whose text cannot be
read would assert what cannot be verified (TODO attach-private-sources).
visibility: public -- this repository is world-readable, and AGENTS.md's
generated loader block is a tracked file, so whatever the block contains
is PUBLISHED, permanently. tools/build_views.py reads this field and
excludes every PRIVATE-level source -- team and individual -- from the
block for that reason. Universal is this repo itself and repo-local lives
in this repo's own tree, so both are already public; team and individual
sets are private repositories whose practice text has never been
published, and rendering their Rule clauses into a tracked file is
publication by another route. Declaring a team source's NAME here in the
open (as this repo does) is not the same disclosure as publishing its
contents. See decisions/2026-09-06-precedent-binds-itself.md section 2,
which rejected multi-source generated views HERE on exactly this ground
and built not_binding instead. The multi-source loader block is still
the right behaviour in a repo that declares several sources and cannot
merge them first, which is why the engine does it and this one field
turns it off here. Verified after the rollout: a CONSUMING repo is not
that case -- precedent_sync_views.py materializes every source into one
practices/ tree before build_views.py sees it, so every consumer's block
was already multi-source. This repo is the only one that cannot take
that route, because its practices/ IS the universal source.
OMITTING this field counts as PUBLIC (build_views.py's repo_is_public),
which reverses what this comment used to say. It claimed an absent
field excluded no source, 'the right default for a private repo'. That
was wrong in the direction that cannot be undone: omitting it is
exactly how a public repo publishes private practice text by accident,
permanently. Found 2026-09-07 in a real public consumer that had never
declared the field and carried 50 private-level practices in its
tracked tree, one of them a person's name and email address. The
opposite error -- declared public, actually private -- costs a few
practices that do not materialize, visible at once and fixed by one
line. A private repo should still DECLARE `visibility: private` rather
than rely on the default, and an undeclared repo is told on stderr
what was assumed.
_filename_separator_comment: Groups where a mixed word separator is correct because NO name in the
group was chosen here (practice: filename-separator). The reason is
mandatory -- an exemption nobody argued for is the silence the check
replaces -- and the check ignores an entry without one.
templates/*.template: each file is named after the file it GENERATES.
pull_request_template.md is GitHub's required filename, and
leak-blocklist.txt is the leak gate's. Renaming either would break the
thing that reads it, to make a folder listing tidier.

filename_separator_exempt.reason: each is named after the file it generates; those names are set by GitHub and by the leak gate, not here

_grandfathered_commit_shas_comment: Commits exempted from the shared check_session_trailer.py, which
the very deep check runs against this repository from the
precedent-shared-repo-maintenance source (its CHECK COVERAGE
section, 'other sources' checks'). Each carries its own note.
They are published history, and rewriting it to quiet a check is
what no-rewrite-for-warnings forbids; the check's own Install
names this list as the remedy. Every commit made after them is
still fully checked.
Eight are watermark commits: the tool that wrote them put no
trailer on anything until 2026-09-28, and now writes the
practice's explicit opt-out (or PRECEDENT_SESSION_URL when a
session hands one over). The rest are sessions that forgot.
THE SAME KEY IS READ BY tools/checks/check_commit_author.py,
check_buenos_aires_dates.py and very_deep_check.py's commit-
identity window, so an entry here exempts that commit from those
too. Measured before adding these: check_commit_author.py passed
on this history, so none of its findings is hidden. Two of them
are Morgan's with a -0400 offset (2026-09-25, the evening commits
here took the repository's fallback zone), which the very deep
check's date read will no longer list.

_source_purpose_comment: One disambiguating sentence per declared source, for a session sorting
where a practice belongs -- added 2026-09-19 after `push-back` was found
sitting in precedent-team-writing (a subject-scoped writing/formatting
set) when its actual subject is contested reasoning in general, not
writing craft. These are read alongside the 'sources' array below;
they do not affect resolution and nothing parses them.
precedent (universal): practices every session everywhere follows --
core, claimed behavior of the system itself, not one team's taste.
precedent-team-writing: the craft of writing and formatting prose for a
human reader only -- citations, lists, emphasis, document mechanics.
Never the substance of an argument or a decision.
precedent-team-repo-maintenance: how to run and maintain a repository
that vendors this practice layer -- syncs, installs, gates, branch and
vendoring conventions. Binds repos of that kind, not people.
precedent-team-working-style: how a session paces, communicates and
hands off work with the person it works for -- registers, escalation,
reporting up the chain. Not writing craft and not repo mechanics.
precedent-individual: one person's own standing preferences -- timezone,
git identity, personal repo conventions, register -- that follow them
into every project, not a team's shared rule.
_adapters_comment: The harness adapters this source installs into every consuming repo's
.claude/hooks/ on each sync (spec/SOURCES.md, 'Harness adapters travel
with the source'). Declared 2026-09-14, closing TODO.md's
universal-adapters-undeclared: until then they were installed by hand and
drifted silently, which is the failure the mechanism was built for.
FIVE, AND THE TWO THAT ARE MISSING ARE THE INTERESTING PART.
templates/harness/claude-code/hooks/ holds eight files.
individual-source-bootstrap.sh.template is not an adapter at all: it
carries variables that tools/precedent_bootstrap_source.py
--write-session-hook substitutes at install time, so copying it verbatim
installs a hook with placeholders where its values belong. A template is
not a derived artifact until something derives it.
commit-identity.sh and freshness-guard.sh are REAL adapters and are still
not declared here, because the individual source already declares the same
two destinations and precedent_materialize.py REFUSES a destination
collision outright -- 'declared as a harness adapter destination by both
...'. Declaring them here would not fight the individual set for the file;
it would break the sync of every repo that has both sources. Measured
2026-09-14 against the real four-source pipeline, after declaring all
seven and watching the consumer case fail.
The individual set is also the right owner of those two: both write a
PERSON's identity or their clone's freshness, and the individual set is
where a person's own values live. Universal keeps the five that are about
the engine rather than about whoever is running it.
THE WIRING DOES NOT TRAVEL AND CANNOT. materialize writes the script and
refuses to touch a consumer's settings.json -- copying that would silently
repoint its base branch. So a repo that does not want one of these ends up
holding an unwired script, which is a legitimate state and is declared
rather than argued about: declined_adapters, with a reason, read by
precedent_check.py's hooks-on-disk-are-reachable.
precedent-universal-catalogue.sh is the one that will be declined most. It
puts the universal catalogue in front of a session rooted in a practice
SET, and an ordinary consuming repo has no such job -- it should decline
that one and say so, rather than wire a hook with nothing to do.
